question: What happens inside cells during degenerative disorders?

options.B: Faulty proteins build up and cause cell death
options.D: Extra protective brain chemicals are produced

explanation: Genetic changes mess up how proteins are made and cleared out, leading to toxic buildup and cell damage. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h1)

question: Why is functional loss in inherited degenerative conditions usually permanent?

options.A: Nerve and muscle cells do not easily regenerate
options.C: Routine tests kill off healthy cells

explanation: Specialized cells like neurons and muscle fibers cannot easily replace themselves once they are damaged. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h1)

question: Which test is used to confirm an inherited degenerative disorder?
explanation: Genetic testing looks for the specific gene changes that cause hereditary conditions. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h2)

question: Why do doctors order an MRI for patients with degenerative disorders?

options.D: To look for brain or tissue shrinkage

explanation: Imaging scans show how tissues and brain structures shrink and deteriorate as the disease progresses. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h2)

question: What is the main goal of nursing care for patients with degenerative disorders?

options.A: Keeping them comfortable and as independent as possible
options.B: Curing the disease within six months
options.C: Preventing family members from getting sick

explanation: Because these conditions have no cure, care focuses on comfort, daily function, and quality of life. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h3)

question: Why is a team of different specialists needed for inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: Therapists take over all nursing duties
options.B: The disease affects multiple body systems at once
options.D: Doctors are not allowed to prescribe alone

explanation: Patients face physical, thinking, and feeding challenges that require different experts working together. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of drugs given for degenerative disorders?

options.D: To ease symptoms and slow down decline

explanation: Medications help manage problems like stiffness or mood changes rather than fixing the root genetic cause. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h4)

question: Why should nurses watch patients with neurodegenerative conditions closely for drug side effects?

options.A: Drug doses are always ten times higher
options.B: They break down all oral drugs faster
options.C: They are often extra sensitive to nervous system drugs
options.D: Pharmacies always give out expired drugs

explanation: Damaged nerve pathways make these patients more prone to bad reactions from medications. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h4)

question: How does an occupational therapist usually help a patient?

options.D: Suggesting tools to help with daily tasks

explanation: Occupational therapists help patients find ways to manage everyday self-care when physical skills fade. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h5)

question: Why is physical therapy important in progressive degenerative conditions?

options.B: It helps prevent tight joints and stiffness
options.C: It replaces the need for any medicine

explanation: Regular movement keeps joints flexible and prevents muscles from shortening despite the disease. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h5)

question: What is the biggest danger of swallowing problems in degenerative disorders?

options.B: Lung infections from choking and poor nutrition
options.C: Loss of the sense of taste

explanation: Trouble swallowing can cause food to go into the lungs or lead to poor calorie intake. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h6)

question: In what position should a patient with swallowing difficulties sit during meals?
explanation: Sitting upright uses gravity to guide food safely down the throat instead of into the airway. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h6)

question: How does genetic counseling help family members?

options.C: By explaining how the disease is inherited and the risks

explanation: Counselors explain family health patterns so relatives understand how a gene change might affect them. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h7)

question: Why is emotional support important for families dealing with degenerative disorders?

options.C: Family members refuse to learn care skills
options.D: They deal with ongoing grief as their loved one declines

explanation: Watching someone slowly lose their abilities causes deep emotional stress that needs compassionate support. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h7)

question: What is the main focus of palliative care for end-stage degenerative illness?

options.A: Trying to cure the terminal illness
options.C: Testing new drugs in clinical trials
options.D: Ensuring comfort and managing final symptoms

explanation: Palliative care centers on relieving pain and keeping the patient comfortable and dignified at the end of life. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h8)

question: When is the best time to talk about living wills and end-of-life wishes with a patient?

options.A: While the patient can still communicate their choices
options.C: Right after telling them the disease is terminal

explanation: Early talks ensure that the patient's own wishes guide their care decisions before they lose the ability to speak. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h8)
